_meta.name: Commodore 64 Resource Catalog
_meta.purpose: Source manifest for Claude Code to ingest into c64-kb for normalization, graph construction, and code archaeology workflows.
_meta.generated_for: Duncan / c64-kb (sister project to pcf-kb, complementary to Rosetta64)

fetch_strategies.wiki_scrape: Recursive scrape with link graph extraction (DokuWiki/MediaWiki). Respect robots.txt; rate-limit 1 req/sec.
fetch_strategies.ftp_mirror: Use lftp/wget mirror; preserve directory structure. Large.
fetch_strategies.git_clone: Clone repo; index README, source comments, docs/, examples/.
fetch_strategies.static_html: Single-page or small site; fetch + readability extract.
fetch_strategies.blog_archive: Walk archive index, fetch posts, extract markdown.
fetch_strategies.db_dump: Pre-built SQLite/MDB available; ingest schema directly.
fetch_strategies.csdb_api: CSDb supports CSV/XML exports per release; scrape release detail pages.
fetch_strategies.pdf_corpus: Bulk PDF download; OCR if scanned; chunk by section.
fetch_strategies.manual_curate: Forum/dynamic; selective extraction of high-signal threads/posts.

entity_types_to_extract: technique (raster bar, sprite multiplexing, FLD/FLI, etc.)
file_format (D64, T64, PRG, SID, CRT, etc.)

_meta.deduplication_note: Many resources mirror each other (e.g., bombjack.org mirrors much of zimmers + project64). Prefer canonical sources where flagged; cross-link the rest.

resources.name: Codebase 64
resources.description: The canonical programming reference wiki for C64. Sections: base (general), VIC programming, SID programming, CIA programming, IO, maths, game programming, demo programming, cross-development. Source-code-heavy.
resources.ingest_notes: DokuWiki. Use ?do=index to enumerate. Code blocks inside <pre class="code 6502"> — extract as first-class entities. Many pages cite authors by CSDb handle; cross-reference with CSDb person entries.

resources.name: C64-Wiki (English)
resources.description: MediaWiki-based general encyclopedia covering hardware, software, games, peripherals, BASIC commands, KERNAL routines, motherboards. English and German parallel wikis.
resources.ingest_notes: Use MediaWiki API (api.php) for clean structured exports. Categories provide good taxonomy.

resources.name: Zimmers.net CBM Archive
resources.description: Bo Zimmerman's archive — schematics, service manuals, ROM dumps, datasheets, magazines, source code, programming references. Mirror of much of the CBM preservation corpus.
resources.ingest_notes: Large (~tens of GB). Mirror /pub/cbm/. Key subtrees: schematics/computers/c64/, magazines/, manuals/, src/, programming/. Most content is decades-stable; one-time mirror sufficient with periodic delta sync.

resources.name: C64 Schematics (Zimmers)
resources.description: All known C64 motherboard schematic revisions: 326298 (Rev A), 250407, 250425, 250441, 250469 (C64C). Plus SX-64, peripherals, power supplies. Service Manual PN-314001-02 included.
resources.ingest_notes: Index by PCB assembly number → schematic number → revision. Cross-reference with C64-Wiki motherboard pages.

resources.name: C64 Service Manual (HTML, Zimmers mirror)
resources.description: Sami Rautiainen's HTML transcription of the Feb 1985 C64 Service Manual. Covers all circuit theory (clock, address decoding, VIC/SID/CIA interconnect, power supply, cassette, paddle/joystick interfaces).

resources.name: C64 Service Manual PDF (314001-02)
resources.description: Official Commodore C64 Service Manual PN-314001-02, September 1985. PDF form. Chip-level circuit theory, troubleshooting, parts list.

resources.name: The MOS 6567/6569 video controller (VIC-II) and its application in the Commodore 64
resources.description: Christian Bauer's exhaustive VIC-II reverse-engineering and reference. THE definitive document on the video chip — register-by-register, cycle-by-cycle behavior including bad lines, badline conditions, sprite DMA, the sequencer.
resources.ingest_notes: Plain text. Sectioned (1–9). Extract as: chip→registers→bits→behavior. Cite as foundational reference for any VIC-II claim.

resources.name: MonkeySpeak: Commodore 64 Hardware Details
resources.description: Curated chip-by-chip reference for Assy 250407 (Schematic 251138): datasheets for 6510, 6526, 6581, 6567/6569, PLA, 4164 DRAM, 74LSxx glue logic, 556 timer, 7406, 7407, 7415. Links to multi-vendor datasheets.
resources.ingest_notes: Excellent cross-reference for chip-vendor variants. Author built it while writing an emulator — verify pin assignments noted as buggy in original schematics.

resources.name: pagetable.com (Michael Steil)
resources.description: Michael Steil's deep-dive blog. C64 KERNAL/BASIC ROM disassembly, history of CBM 8-bit ROMs, PLA internals, 6502 quirks, fastloaders. Highly cited.
resources.ingest_notes: WordPress archive (/year/month/). Many posts have downloadable artifacts (disassemblies, tools).

resources.name: C64 KERNAL Disassembly (mist64)
resources.description: Michael Steil's curated original source code archive for CBM 8-bit ROMs: PET, VIC-20, C64, C128 KERNALs and BASIC. Reconstructed from leaked Commodore sources where possible.
resources.ingest_notes: Source is well-commented and label-named. Ideal for grounding KERNAL routine entries ($FF81–$FFFB jump table).

resources.name: Ultimate Commodore 64 Reference (mist64)
resources.description: Merged C64 reference: ROM disassembly + complete memory map + KERNAL/BASIC API + 6502/6510 opcodes. Multi-source aggregation rendered as cross-referenced HTML.
resources.ingest_notes: Already partially normalized — use as schema model. Convertible to graph trivially.

resources.name: 6502.org
resources.description: CPU-level reference for 6502 family: opcodes, undocumented instructions, timing, source code archive (tutorials, libraries, projects). Not C64-specific but foundational.
resources.ingest_notes: Subtrees: tutorials/, source/, documents/. Cross-link with C64-specific 6510 quirks.

resources.name: The Fridge (ffd2.com)
resources.description: Long-standing code repository for C64 and 6502 programmers. Routines, snippets, demo source contributions.
resources.ingest_notes: Older site; categorize as historical-corpus.

resources.name: All About Your 64
resources.description: Ninja/The Dreams' classic online help (1995–2005) — A-Z reference covering BASIC commands, KERNAL calls, hardware registers.

resources.name: Project 64 (text manuals)
resources.description: Volunteer project converting CBM manuals, books, magazines to ASCII/text. Now largely mirrored at bombjack.org.

resources.name: DLH's Commodore Archive (bombjack.org)
resources.description: Massive PDF archive — books, magazines (RUN, COMPUTE!, COMPUTE!'s Gazette, Ahoy!, Zzap!64), manuals, brochures, datasheets, schematics. Covers C64, C128, VIC-20, +4, Amiga.
resources.ingest_notes: Several TB if mirrored fully. Be selective: C64 books + Programmer's Reference Guide + Compute!'s Gazette is the high-signal subset for code archaeology.

resources.name: Commodore 64 Programmer's Reference Guide
resources.description: The bible. Official 1982 Commodore reference: BASIC, KERNAL, sprites, sound, hardware. Includes the (known-buggy) schematic. Essential normalization anchor.

resources.name: Mapping the Commodore 64 (Sheldon Leemon)
resources.description: Address-by-address C64 memory map ($0000–$FFFF). The reference for what every byte does. COMPUTE! Books, 1984.

resources.name: CSDb — The C-64 Scene Database
resources.description: Definitive database of C64 demoscene productions: demos, intros, music, gfx, tools, cracks, magazines. Plus releases, groups, sceners (people), events, party results, votes, forum.
resources.ingest_notes: Per-release URLs: /release/?id=N. Per-group: /group/?id=N. Per-person: /scener/?id=N. No formal public API but stable HTML with consistent class names. Releases include credits as structured rows — extract as (release, role, scener) triples. ~150K releases as of 2024.

resources.name: GameBase64
resources.description: Definitive C64 games database. ~30,000 entries (v19, 2023) with screenshots, music (SID), magazine reviews, cover scans, longplays. Disk images included.
resources.ingest_notes: Distributed as MS Access MDB (Jet) or SQLite (community port). Direct DB dump avoids scraping. SQLite mirror: twinbirds.com/gamebase64browser. Schema is stable across versions.

resources.name: Lemon64
resources.description: ~9,700 game database + active forum. Forum (phpBB) is goldmine for current C64 dev discussion (cross-assemblers, fastloaders, hardware Q&A).
resources.ingest_notes: Forum subforums: 'Commodore 64' (general), 'New releases'. Threads are densely technical — selective ingestion by thread tags.

resources.name: Forum64.de
resources.description: Largest German-language C64 community. Strong hardware/repair coverage, also dev discussion.
resources.ingest_notes: German. Use language detection in normalization. Hardware repair threads often have schematics and oscilloscope traces not found elsewhere.

resources.name: Plus/4 World
resources.description: Sister site to CSDb for the C16/C116/Plus/4 family. Tool documentation (e.g., Krill's Loader) is often shared across platforms.
resources.ingest_notes: Flag entries that cross-target C64 (many tools do).

resources.name: Scenebase
resources.description: Bulk disk image archive, including cracker/scene group disk packages.

resources.name: C64 Preservation Project
resources.description: Preserves original, uncracked disk images with copy protection intact. G64 format. Pete Rittwage's project.
resources.ingest_notes: Important for understanding original loaders and protection schemes — vital for code archaeology.

resources.name: FUNET CBM archive
resources.description: Finnish university FTP — long-standing CBM corpus. Overlaps with Zimmers but has unique programming sub-archives.
resources.ingest_notes: Cross-dedupe with Zimmers.

resources.name: Pouet.net
resources.description: Cross-platform demoscene database. C64 prods filterable. Useful for cross-references when a coder works on multiple platforms.
resources.ingest_notes: Filter platform=Commodore 64. Crosslink CSDb IDs where present in prod comments.

resources.name: Demozoo
resources.description: Modern cross-platform demoscene database with cleaner data model than Pouet. Has an actual JSON API.
resources.ingest_notes: https://demozoo.org/api/v1/ — productions, parties, releasers all queryable. Great normalization target/reference.

resources.name: scene.org
resources.description: Authoritative file archive for demoscene productions across platforms, including C64 (search /demos/groups/, /parties/).

resources.name: Recollection (Atlantis Prophecy)
resources.description: C64 demoscene 'oldschool magazine' covering history, world firsts, world records, interviews. Curated by sceners — high signal.
resources.ingest_notes: World Firsts list (?load=world_of_demos) is a structured taxonomy of demoscene techniques and their attribution.

resources.name: High Voltage SID Collection (HVSC)
resources.description: The canonical SID music corpus. ~58,000+ tunes as of 2024. Standardized .sid format with PSID/RSID headers. STIL (SID Tune Information List) provides metadata: composer, year, source release.
resources.ingest_notes: Distributed as ~250MB zip. STIL.txt and SongLengths.md5 are structured metadata files — parse those first; they cross-reference releases to composers.

resources.name: Compute's Gazette SID Collection (CGSC)
resources.description: Companion to HVSC focused on SID music from COMPUTE!'s Gazette magazine listings.

resources.name: DeepSID
resources.description: JCH/Vibrants' modern web-based SID player. Source on GitHub. Pulls from HVSC + CGSC. Useful for embedding in c64-kb UI.
resources.ingest_notes: https://github.com/Chordian/deepsid — reference implementation for streaming SID over the web.

resources.name: GoatTracker 2
resources.description: Lasse Öörni's cross-platform C64 SID tracker. Uses reSID. De facto standard tracker for non-native composition. .sng format.
resources.ingest_notes: Author 'Cadaver' is also author of multiple other C64 tools — cross-link as person entity.

resources.name: SID-Wizard
resources.description: Hermit's native C64 tracker. Stereo (2SID/3SID) support. XM/MIDI/GoatTracker conversion. MIDI hardware support. Janko keyboard layout option.

resources.name: DefMon
resources.description: Cadaver's older native-C64 tracker. Lower-level than GoatTracker — used by many demoscene composers.

resources.name: SID Factory II
resources.description: Chordian's cross-platform SID composer designed around JCH/Vibrants player concepts. Modern alternative to GoatTracker.

resources.name: reSID (Dag Lem)
resources.description: C++ library — cycle-accurate SID 6581/8580 emulation. Underlies VICE audio, GoatTracker, and most SID players.

resources.name: JSIDPlay2
resources.description: Java SID player with full C64 emulation back-end. Reference player implementation.

resources.name: SID Known (Wilfred Bos)
resources.description: CLI tool to identify SID tunes from .sid or .prg files against the HVSC corpus. Hash-based matching.

resources.name: VICE — Versatile Commodore Emulator
resources.description: The canonical multi-platform CBM emulator (C64, C128, VIC-20, PET, Plus/4, CBM-II). Built-in monitor/debugger, remote monitor over TCP, x64sc cycle-accurate mode. Source is itself documentation.
resources.ingest_notes: Source includes invaluable comments on hardware quirks. Monitor protocol (binary + text) is documented in vice.pdf — ingest as the spec for programmatic debugging.

resources.name: VICE Binary Monitor Protocol
resources.description: Documentation of VICE's binary monitor protocol — enables external tools/IDEs to drive VICE for automated testing, code archaeology, and remote inspection.

resources.name: VirtualC64 (Dirk Hoffmann)
resources.description: macOS-native C64 emulator with strong debugging UI and visual chip inspectors. Source is well-commented Swift/C++.

resources.name: Denise (cycle-accurate multi-platform debugger emu)
resources.description: Cycle-accurate debugger-focused emulator covering C64, Atari, NES, GB. Strong code archaeology tool.

resources.name: RetroDebugger (slajerek)
resources.description: Modern integrated debugger for C64/Atari/NES wrapping VICE/Atari800. Memory/register/PC inspectors.

resources.name: C64 Debugger (Mihail Slavutskii / slajerek)
resources.description: Predecessor / sibling to RetroDebugger. Used widely in C64 dev community.

resources.name: Kick Assembler
resources.description: Java-based 6502 cross-assembler by Mads Nielsen (Camelot). High-level features (macros, scripting, math, PNG-to-data import) make it the demoscene favorite.
resources.ingest_notes: Manual is a substantial reference doc — extract macro/directive reference.

resources.name: ACME Cross-Assembler
resources.description: Long-running open-source 6502/65816 cross-assembler. Strong codebase64 community usage.

resources.name: 64tass (Turbo Assembler Macro)
resources.description: Modern descendant of the native C64 Turbo Assembler syntax. Strong nested-scope support.

resources.name: cc65 (C Compiler + ca65 assembler suite)
resources.description: ISO-C compiler + ca65 macro assembler + ld65 linker + librarian. Targets C64, C128, Atari, NES, Apple II, and dozens of others. The lingua franca of 6502 C development.
resources.ingest_notes: Includes target-specific config files and libraries (e.g., c64.cfg, joystick drivers, conio.h) which document memory layout assumptions.

resources.name: Oscar64
resources.description: Optimizing C/C++ cross-compiler for 6502 (drmortalwombat). Generates significantly tighter code than cc65 in many benchmarks. Targets C64, C128, CRT, NES.

resources.name: LLVM-MOS
resources.description: LLVM backend for 6502 family. Modern Clang/LLVM toolchain — C/C++/Rust. LTO, GNU-compatible assembler/linker. Targets C64, NES, Atari, Apple II, X16, more.

resources.name: DASM
resources.description: Matt Dillon's venerable 6502 assembler. Popular for Atari 2600 but also used for C64.

resources.name: xa (Floodgap)
resources.description: Multi-pass cross-assembler for 6502 series and 65816. Cameron Kaiser's maintenance branch.

resources.name: TMPx
resources.description: Cross-platform port of Turbo Macro Pro (native C64 TMP). Preserves TMP syntax.

resources.name: MADS (Mad Assembler)
resources.description: FreePascal 6502/65816 portable assembler. Atari-leaning but C64-capable.

resources.name: vasm/vbcc
resources.description: Modular cross-assembler supporting 6502 among many CPUs.

resources.name: VS64 (VSCode extension)
resources.description: VSCode extension orchestrating ACME / Kick Assembler / cc65 / LLVM-MOS / Oscar64 / BASIC. Project config schema, build, debug via VICE.
resources.ingest_notes: project-config.json schema is a useful normalization model for build-config entities.

resources.name: Relaunch64
resources.description: Java cross-platform editor for 64tass, ACME, ca65, DASM, DreamAss, Kick Assembler, TMPx. Syntax highlighting + build.

resources.name: CBM .prg Studio
resources.description: Windows IDE for C64/VIC-20/C128/Plus-4 BASIC + assembly. Includes sprite/char editors, screen designer.

resources.name: C64 Studio (Georg Rottensteiner)
resources.description: Windows IDE for BASIC and assembly. Sprite editor, charset editor, map editor included. ACME-syntax-based.

resources.name: 8bitworkshop
resources.description: Browser-based 8-bit development IDE with emulator and tutorials. Covers C64 among many platforms. Steven Hugg.

resources.name: c64lib (Maciej Małecki)
resources.description: KickAssembler library suite: chipset (VIC/CIA), text macros, raster handling (Copper64), bootstrapping, Gradle build plugin. Modular.

resources.name: LAMAlib (cc65 macro library)
resources.description: Lightweight Assembler MAcro library for cc65/ca65. High-level macros for game/demo development.

resources.name: Millfork
resources.description: High-level language targeting 6502 family (and others). Better code generation than C in many cases. Native C64 target.

resources.name: ugBASIC
resources.description: Isomorphic BASIC compiler — same source compiles to C64, ZX Spectrum, Atari 8-bit, MSX, Amiga, etc.

resources.name: XC=BASIC
resources.description: Structured BASIC compiler for CBM 8-bit. Compiles to native 6502 assembly.

resources.name: CharPad
resources.description: Subchrist Software's character set and tile/map editor. De facto standard for char-mode game graphics. Free version + Pro version. .ctm format.

resources.name: SpritePad
resources.description: Subchrist Software's sprite editor (Pro & free). Companion to CharPad. .spd format.

resources.name: Spritemate
resources.description: Browser-based C64 sprite editor by Ingo Hinterding. Exports to multiple formats.

resources.name: lvllvl
resources.description: Browser-based collaborative character-set art creation.

resources.name: Marq's PETSCII Editor
resources.description: Cross-platform PETSCII art editor. Outputs source code in multiple assembler dialects.

resources.name: PETSCII.krissz.hu
resources.description: Browser PETSCII editor.

resources.name: Multipaint
resources.description: Multi-platform 8-bit pixel art editor (C64, Spectrum, Plus/4, Amstrad, MSX) respecting color/attribute constraints.

resources.name: RetroPIC
resources.description: Image converter for C64 and other retro machines. PNG/JPG → koala/multicolor/hires.

resources.name: Convertron3000
resources.description: Image converter to C64 formats.

resources.name: Koala Painter format spec
resources.description: Format specification for the dominant C64 bitmap art format ($0801 loader + 10,003-byte payload).

resources.name: Exomizer
resources.description: Magnus Lind's compression tool with C64 decruncher. Best-in-class ratio. Self-extracting PRG mode. Supports backwards/in-place decrunch. v3.x.
resources.ingest_notes: Source includes the C64 ASM decrunchers — useful for code archaeology of crunched releases.

resources.name: PuCrunch (Pasi Ojala)
resources.description: Classic C64 LZ-variant cruncher. Faster decrunch than Exomizer; slightly larger output. Public domain.

resources.name: ByteBoozer 2 / B2 (HCL)
resources.description: HCL/Booze Design cruncher. Fast decrunch, used in many demos.

resources.name: TSCrunch (Antonio Savona)
resources.description: Fast decompression cruncher — faster than Exomizer/PuCrunch, similar ratio.

resources.name: Doynamite / Doynax LZ
resources.description: Doynax's LZ compressor with tiny C64 decruncher. Used for tight intros.

resources.name: Subsizer
resources.description: Compression tool focused on small payloads.

resources.name: Dali / Level Crusher
resources.description: LZ-class compressors suited for small data blocks (level data, in-game streaming).

resources.name: Krill's Loader
resources.description: Krill/Plush's IRQ-driven fast loader. Wide device support (1541/71/81, SD2IEC, Ultimate, etc.). De facto standard. Source includes integrated decruncher hooks for Exomizer/Doynax/B2.
resources.ingest_notes: Repository version numbering (V166, V184, etc.) tracks releases. Source is extensively commented.

resources.name: Spindle (Lft)
resources.description: Linus Åkesson's loader/scheduler for trackmos. Sector-precise loading scheduled with effect timing. Used in many recent record-breaking demos.
resources.ingest_notes: Documentation explains GCR on-the-fly decoding — pair with codebase64 fastloaders page.

resources.name: Bitfire
resources.description: Bbox/Bonzai's IRQ loader optimized for trackmos. Drive-side block tracking.

resources.name: Sparkle (Sparta)
resources.description: Sparta's modern trackmo loader. Used by Offence, Resource and others.

resources.name: Bongo
resources.description: Earlier trackmo loader. Historical reference.

resources.name: lft on GCR (pagetable)
resources.description: Discussion/explanation of Linus Åkesson's GCR on-the-fly decoding scheme used in Spindle and Bitfire — foundational reading for understanding modern C64 fastloaders.

resources.name: Covert Bitops (Cadaver) loaders + tools
resources.description: Lasse Öörni's collection: IRQ loader, MW disk transfer, game engines (Steel Ranger, Hessian, Mermaid), and more. Source-available.

resources.name: Spindle ecosystem (Lft software)
resources.description: Lft's full toolset: Spindle, SymbiOS sound engine, Chipdisko player, qmeg. Several novel approaches documented in detail.

resources.name: Oxyron 'Optimizing for speed' (codebase64 mirror)
resources.description: Classic 6502/6510 optimization tricks compendium — illegal opcodes, cycle-counting, self-modifying patterns, page-boundary tricks.

resources.name: VIC-II undocumented behavior compendium
resources.description: Codebase64 catalog of VIC-II tricks: open borders, FLD (Flexible Line Distance), FLI (Flexible Line Interpretation), FPP (Flexible Pixel Position), DMA delay, line crunch.

resources.name: VIC-II die shots & reverse engineering
resources.description: visual6502 project — high-resolution VIC-II die shots, transistor-level analysis. Pair with Christian Bauer's behavior doc for complete chip understanding.

resources.name: Visual 6502
resources.description: Transistor-level simulation and die shots of 6502 (and 6510 by extension). Authoritative source for CPU microarchitecture details, including undocumented opcode behavior.

resources.name: No More Secrets — PLA decapping
resources.description: 906114-01 PLA (82S100) equations and dumps. Critical for emulator accuracy and homebrew replacements.

resources.name: Pictorial C64 Fault Guide
resources.description: Pictorial step-by-step C64 fault diagnosis.

resources.name: Ray Carlsen C64 Tech Notes
resources.description: Long-standing repair guide collection from one of the most respected C64 hardware technicians.

resources.name: World of Jani (rump.dk)
resources.description: Jani's deep-dive coding write-ups. Sprite multiplexing, raster routines, FLI variants.

resources.name: 64bites
resources.description: Paid video tutorial series by Krzysztof Studzinski — modern C64 dev from basics through demo coding. Companion materials sometimes free.

resources.name: Retro Game Dev (Derek Morris)
resources.description: Modern book series on C64 game development using CBM .prg Studio (assembly). Companion site with code.

resources.name: COMPUTE!'s Gazette archive
resources.description: Internet Archive collection of COMPUTE!'s Gazette — most influential C64 type-in/programming magazine. ~6 years, machine-language listings.

resources.name: Zzap!64 archive
resources.description: Definitive UK C64 magazine. Reviews, interviews, programming tutorials, scene coverage.

resources.name: RUN Magazine archive
resources.description: US C64/C128 programming magazine.

resources.name: Ahoy! Magazine archive
resources.description: Early US CBM magazine covering VIC-20 and C64.

resources.name: Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit (SEUCK)
resources.description: 1987 game construction kit by Sensible Software. Still actively used by community — 'SEUCK Compo' annual. SEUCK Redux modernizes it.

resources.name: SEUCK Redux (TND)
resources.description: Richard Bayliss / TND's modernized SEUCK with parallax, music, expanded features.

resources.name: Elite (C64) commented disassembly — markmoxon
resources.description: Mark Moxon's exhaustively commented disassemblies of Elite across multiple platforms, including C64. Excellent reference for code archaeology methodology and Rosetta64 cross-platform Elite comparisons.
resources.ingest_notes: Same author maintains parallel BBC/Acorn/NES disassemblies — comparison enables cross-port study.

resources.name: Elite C64 CA65 disassembly
resources.description: CA65-assemblable Elite C64 source — recompilable from original Ian Bell / David Braben binary.

resources.name: GitHub Topic: c64 / commodore-64 / commodore64
resources.description: GitHub topic indexes — running discovery surface for new tools, disassemblies, libraries. Crawl monthly.
resources.ingest_notes: Use GitHub API (search/repositories?q=topic:c64) to enumerate; filter by stars/recent-push for signal.

resources.name: vigo/awesome-c64
resources.description: Curated awesome-list. Thin but historically useful pointers.

resources.name: mcicolella/awesome-commodore-resources
resources.description: Curated list including blogs, books, communities, tools — Italian-leaning but useful for community linkage.

resources.name: mist64 GitHub repos (CBM history & ROMs)
resources.description: Michael Steil's collected CBM 8-bit reverse engineering: cbmsrc, c64ref, c64rom, msbasic, mega65-rom, plus cross-platform ROM tools.
resources.ingest_notes: Treat as a meta-source — clone each repo and index. Author cross-link to pagetable.com.

resources.name: Stadium64
resources.description: Screenshots and brief reviews of C64 games.

resources.name: Intros.c64.org
resources.description: Archive of crack intros — historical artifact rich in scene group attribution.

resources.name: C64.sk
resources.description: C64 news portal — release announcements, scene coverage.

resources.name: Commodore.software
resources.description: Software archive — commercial games, productivity, tools. Wider scope than scene archives.

resources.name: C64 Longplays
resources.description: Video longplays of C64 games. Useful for behavior reference when reverse-engineering.

resources.name: D64 / G64 / T64 / TAP / CRT / SID format specs
resources.description: Peter Schepers' authoritative CBM file format specs: D64, G64, NIB, T64, TAP, P00, CRT, REL, SID, P00. The reference for any tool reading/writing C64 disk/tape/cart images.

resources.name: VICE disk/tape format documentation
resources.description: VICE's documentation for all supported file formats. Complements Schepers.

resources.name: C64 cartridge format reference (CRT)
resources.description: Cartridge image (CRT) format with chip-by-chip layout, supported cart types (Magic Desk, Ocean, EasyFlash, Final Cartridge III, etc.).

resources.name: Ultimate 64 / 1541 Ultimate REST API
resources.description: Documentation for Gideon Zweijtzer's Ultimate 64 / Ultimate II+ REST API — modern hardware programmable from the network.

resources.name: MEGA65 documentation
resources.description: MEGA65 (modern reimplementation of unreleased C65) docs — useful for context when C64 enhancements/successors come up in code archaeology.

resources.name: TheC64 / TheC64 Mini
resources.description: Retro Games Ltd's modern C64 replica. Reference only for cross-platform release targets.

resources.name: Lemon64 'C64 Acid Tests' / VIC-II compatibility tests
resources.description: VIC-II/SID/CIA compatibility tests used to evaluate emulator/clone accuracy. Each test is a documented edge case.

resources.name: DirMaster
resources.description: Style64's GUI tool for managing D64/D71/D81/D82/G64 disk images. Drag-drop PRG, BAM editing.

resources.name: cbmconvert
resources.description: CLI tool for converting between CBM file formats (PRG, P00, T64, D64, ARK, LNX, etc.). Useful for ingestion pipelines.

resources.name: petcat (VICE)
resources.description: VICE's PRG-to-BASIC-text and reverse converter. Essential for ingesting BASIC programs from PRG corpora.

resources.name: Regenerator
resources.description: PRG to ACME-syntax assembly disassembler with smart labeling.

resources.name: Ghidra MOS 65xx loader
resources.description: Ghidra has 6502/6510 support via SLEIGH. Use with C64 memory map overlay for full reverse engineering workflow. Pairs naturally with Rosetta64.

resources.name: C64 disassembly tools (community)
resources.description: Survey of C64 disassemblers (Regenerator, dxa, da65, Ghidra SLEIGH, IDA loaders).

resources.name: da65 (cc65 disassembler)
resources.description: cc65's disassembler — produces ca65-assemblable source. Info-file driven for symbol/region annotation.

resources.name: Wikipedia: Commodore 64
resources.description: Wikipedia's C64 article and related (VIC-II, SID, C64 demos, MOS 6510, Fast loader). Useful for general-knowledge anchoring and citation cross-references.

resources.name: STIL — SID Tune Information List
resources.description: Structured per-tune metadata for HVSC: composer credits, source release, cover history, trivia. Tab/colon delimited — parseable directly into graph.

resources.name: HVSC SongLengths.md5
resources.description: MD5 hash → song length table for HVSC. Identifies tunes by content hash; useful for normalization and cross-referencing.

resources.name: CSDb stats pages (group hierarchies, country, year)
resources.description: CSDb's pre-aggregated views by group, country, year, party. Convenient seeds for graph analysis (group lineages, country-level scene density).

_ingestion_strategy.phase_1_rationale: These provide the schema scaffolding — chips, registers, opcodes, KERNAL routines, memory map, file formats — that every other source will reference. Normalize these first; they become the canonical entities everything else hangs off.
_ingestion_strategy.phase_2_rationale: Now ingest the bulk databases. Each release/tune/game gets a node; metadata from STIL and SongLengths cross-links HVSC tunes to CSDb releases and GB64 games via composer/year.
_ingestion_strategy.phase_3_rationale: Tools have manuals/READMEs that become 'how to use' entities. Source repos contain the canonical decrunchers/loaders that appear in nearly every demoscene release — ingest source so code archaeology can match crunched/loaded payloads to known tool signatures.
_ingestion_strategy.phase_4_rationale: Tie into Rosetta64. Pre-commented disassemblies (Elite, KERNAL, BASIC) are training/grounding data for archaeology agents. The disassembler tools are part of the analysis pipeline itself.
_ingestion_strategy.phase_5_long_tail: Magazines, blogs, forum threads. Lower priority but high value for ground-truth on author intent, period-correct techniques, and the social fabric of the scene. Process via summarization rather than verbatim ingestion.

_de_duplication_aliases.zimmers_mirrors_in_bombjack: Most schematics and books at bombjack.org are also at zimmers.net. Prefer zimmers as canonical for schematics; prefer bombjack for magazines (better scans).
_de_duplication_aliases.hvsc_versus_stil: STIL is a sub-corpus of HVSC. Ingest STIL as structured metadata, not as a separate corpus.
_de_duplication_aliases.cc65_includes_ca65_ld65_da65: These are sub-tools of the cc65 suite. Index as components, not standalone tools.
_de_duplication_aliases.mist64_repos: c64ref, cbmsrc, msbasic, c64rom, etc. are all under github.com/mist64 and share authorship/style. Group as a single source family.

_known_unstable_links.ffd2.com_fridge: HTTP only; archive copy recommended via web.archive.org
